edit.description: Add load-time refusal in loadChainModule (~L678-745), sibling to validateFrictionDeclaration (~L581-601): usage-shaped error for (a) a phase declaring entryChannelPaths without scopeWritesToEntry:true, (b) a concurrency:singleton phase declaring an afterMerge gate.
Add refusal tests for both dead-declaration shapes, mirroring the existing absolute-path friction refusal test (~L7020).

summary: loadChainModule refuses two dead declarations at load: entryChannelPaths w/o scopeWritesToEntry, and an afterMerge gate on a singleton phase

per.section: A dead declaration is refused at load

tests: loadChainModule throws a usage-shaped error naming the field when a phase declares entryChannelPaths without scopeWritesToEntry:true
loadChainModule throws a usage-shaped error naming the gate and phase when a concurrency:singleton phase declares an afterMerge gate
a scoped phase with entryChannelPaths (scopeWritesToEntry:true) and a fanout phase with an afterMerge gate both still load
acceptance: Both dead-declaration shapes throw at loadChainModule with a usage-shaped, field-naming error; the two still-live shapes (entryChannelPaths on a scoped phase; afterMerge on a fanout phase) load unchanged.
notes: Static deadness bar only, per spec. Verified today's runtime evidence both shapes are silently dead: entryChannelPaths only reached via `assignedEntry && phase.scopeWritesToEntry` (Dispatcher.ts:2342-2346); afterMerge gates only filtered inside fanout's per-entry isolation (Dispatcher.ts:1643), never reached by a singleton tick.

edit.description: Add tickTimeoutMs?: number to Chain.supervisorPolicy (~L349-374), sibling to maxParallel; per-tick read, not run-scoped.

Thread chain into runSingleton (~L1283, call site ~L1182). Read chain.supervisorPolicy?.tickTimeoutMs ?? this.tickTimeoutMs at both invokeAgent call sites (~L1345 singleton, ~L2103 fanout — chain already in scope via runFanoutEntry's chain param), mirroring runFanout's maxParallel pattern (~L1509).
Add per-tick tickTimeoutMs override tests (singleton + fanout) and a neither-knob-declared byte-identical-defaults case, mirroring the existing maxParallel test.

summary: Add tickTimeoutMs to Chain.supervisorPolicy; read per-tick (chain.supervisorPolicy?.tickTimeoutMs ?? this.tickTimeoutMs) at both invokeAgent call sites

per.section: Supervisor policy is a chain-overridable default

tests: a chain-declared supervisorPolicy.tickTimeoutMs overrides DispatcherOptions.tickTimeoutMs for a singleton phase's agent invocation
a chain-declared supervisorPolicy.tickTimeoutMs overrides DispatcherOptions.tickTimeoutMs for a fanout entry's agent invocation
a chain declaring neither maxParallel nor tickTimeoutMs still gets the DispatcherOptions defaults, byte-identical
acceptance: invokeAgent's spawned timeoutMs reflects the tick's own resolved chain.supervisorPolicy?.tickTimeoutMs at both call sites, read fresh per tick like maxParallel — not bound once per run like quarantineScope/abortThreshold.
notes: tickTimeoutMs is the existing DispatcherOptions cap (Dispatcher.ts:837,1071,1084,2280-2282), already enforced but until now unreachable from a chain/CLI-driven loop — no runaway brake on autonomous loops. Per-tick scope because nothing accumulates across ticks, unlike quarantine/abort.

per.section: `flume job new <name>` — seed a state root

tests: jobNew logs a next-step line naming `flume job run <name>`
acceptance: flume job new <name>'s final log line names `flume job run <name>` as the next command.
